findings.title: initials returns a string with a lone surrogate
findings.explanation: Every string argument is well formed UTF-16, but the return value contains an unpaired surrogate (U+D83D at index 0). A lone surrogate renders as a replacement character, makes encodeURIComponent throw and is changed by TextEncoder and by JSON round trips through UTF-8. It usually means a string was cut between the two halves of a surrogate pair, for example by slice, substring, substr or a length limit counted in UTF-16 code units.
findings.expected: A well formed string. Cut text at code point or grapheme boundaries so surrogate pairs stay together.

evidence.note: U+D83D at index 0 of the return value has no partner

findings.title: yearLabel returns different results in different time zones
findings.explanation: yearLabel takes no Date and no time zone argument, yet the same call returns a different value when the process runs with TZ=America/Sao_Paulo instead of TZ=UTC. Code like this usually mixes local time getters (getHours, getDate, getFullYear, toLocaleString) with UTC values, so results change near midnight and New Year, or between servers and browsers in different zones.
findings.expected: The same result in every time zone, or an explicit time zone parameter.

findings.title: initials throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toUpperCase')
findings.explanation: The arguments match the declared parameter types (initials(name: string): string), but the call throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toUpperCase'). This message comes from the JavaScript engine, not from an explicit validation check, which usually means the code reads a property of undefined or null, calls a missing method or iterates something that is not iterable.
findings.expected: A return value, or an explicit error that explains which input is not supported (and a declared type that excludes it).

evidence.result: throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toUpperCase')

findings.title: average returns NaN for finite input
findings.explanation: All numeric arguments are finite, but the result is NaN. NaN usually leaks from 0 / 0, Infinity - Infinity, arithmetic on undefined or a failed lookup, and then spreads silently through later calculations.
findings.expected: A finite number, or an explicit error for inputs outside the supported range.

findings.title: label returns different results for the same input
findings.explanation: Calling label twice in a row with the same arguments, in the same process, gave different results. The clock is frozen during the calls and each call gets a fresh copy of the arguments, so the difference comes from somewhere else: Math.random, a module level counter or cache, or other state shared between calls.
findings.expected: The same result for the same arguments, or a name and documentation that make the variation explicit.

findings.title: decodeBase(encodeBase(x)) does not return x
findings.explanation: encodeBase and decodeBase look like inverse functions. For a well formed input x, decodeBase(encodeBase(x)) returned ' ' instead of x. One of the two functions loses information for this input, or the pair is not meant to be inverse (then this finding can be ignored).

findings.title: slugify is not idempotent
findings.explanation: The name suggests a normalizing function, and applying a normalizer twice should change nothing. For this input a second application changed the result again ('x_y' became 'x-y'), so values normalized once and values normalized twice compare as different.

findings.title: formatFixed drops the minus sign of numbers between -1 and 0
findings.explanation: formatFixed(-0.5) returns '0.50', the same as for 0.5. Negative numbers outside that range keep their sign (formatFixed(-1.5) returns '-1.50'), so the sign is lost only when the integer part is zero. This often happens when the integer part is computed first and the sign is read from it: the integer part of -0.5 is -0, which prints as "0".
findings.expected: A result with a minus sign, like '-1.50' for -1.5.

findings.title: percent throws RangeError for some inputs that match its types
findings.explanation: For arguments that match the declared types (percent(part: number, total: number): number), the call throws RangeError: total must not be 0. This looks like an intentional validation error or a documented limit, so it is reported for information only. If the input is not supported, a narrower declared type would let TypeScript users catch it at compile time.
findings.expected: A narrower declared type, or a documented error.

evidence.result: throws RangeError: total must not be 0

findings.title: randomToken returns a different result on each call
findings.explanation: randomToken returned different results for the same arguments. Its name suggests randomness, time or unique ids, so this is likely intended.
findings.expected: The same result for the same arguments, or a name and documentation that make the variation explicit.
